title: Twenty First Word First Station Fourth Warning Prayers Result And Eternal Reward

questions.question: What is the main question raised at the start of this passage about worship?
questions.answer: It asks whether worship really has little benefit and little reward.

questions.question: What example shows that people will work hard for a small worldly reason?
questions.answer: A person may keep working all day for a little money or because of fear.

questions.question: According to the passage, how do the required prayers help a weak heart in this world?
questions.answer: They give it spiritual support and richness.

questions.question: Besides helping in this life, what future places or times are mentioned where prayer will help a person?
questions.answer: It will help in the grave, at the resurrection, and while crossing the Sirat.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s promise compared with a human promise?
questions.answer: A person may break a promise, but Allah never does.

questions.question: Why is it foolish to trust a human promise but act carelessly about Allah’s promise?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s promise is completely true and much greater.

questions.question: What kind of reward is promised for worship?
questions.answer: Paradise and everlasting happiness.

questions.question: How is the time spent in worship described?
questions.answer: It is short, easy, and pleasant.

questions.question: What wrong attitude toward worship is warned against?
questions.answer: Doing it like a burden, with boredom, or without care.

questions.question: What may a person deserve if he treats Allah’s promise lightly and serves unwillingly?
questions.answer: A strong rebuke and a severe punishment.

questions.question: What comparison is made between fear of prison and fear of Hell?
questions.answer: If people can work hard out of fear of prison, they should even more eagerly worship out of fear of Hell.

questions.question: What is one main lesson of the whole passage?
questions.answer: A believer should perform prayer eagerly because its rewards are great, its burden is light, and Allah’s promise is certain.

questions.question: Why does the passage call the inner self foolish?
questions.answer: Because it gets tired of worship even though worship brings huge benefits.

questions.question: What does the example of being paid a little money teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that people often make strong effort for small worldly gain.

questions.question: What does this comparison help us understand about prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer deserves even more effort because its reward is much greater.

questions.question: In this world, what are the prayers said to be for the heart?
questions.answer: They are like provision and treasure for a weak and needy heart.

questions.question: In the grave, what are prayers compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to nourishment and light.

questions.question: On the Day of Judgment, what role do prayers have?
questions.answer: They serve like proof in a person’s favor.

questions.question: On the Sirat, how do prayers help?
questions.answer: They help like light and a ride to carry a person.

questions.question: What is the difference between the man who promises money and Allah, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The man may fail to keep his word, but Allah never fails.

questions.question: Why is half-hearted worship presented as dangerous?
questions.answer: Because it shows disrespect toward Allah’s promise and gift.

questions.question: What does the passage say should motivate a person besides hope for reward?
questions.answer: Fear of punishment in the next life should also motivate him.

questions.question: What balance of feelings does the passage encourage in worship?
questions.answer: It encourages both hope for great reward and fear of serious punishment.

questions.question: What complaint of the self is answered in this passage?
questions.answer: The complaint that worship is tiring and not worth much.

questions.question: What everyday behavior is used to show that people can work hard when they want to?
questions.answer: They will keep working for hours for a small payment or because they feel threatened.

questions.question: What does the passage say prayer gives the heart during life in this world?
questions.answer: It gives spiritual strength and valuable support.

questions.question: How do prayers help a person after death, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They bring help in the grave and on the Day of Judgment.

questions.question: What does the passage say about crossing the Sirat?
questions.answer: It says every person must pass over it.

questions.question: What does this passage suggest about the value of a small amount of worship time?
questions.answer: A short time of worship can bring enormous reward.

questions.question: Why is the promise of eternal happiness more trustworthy than a promise from people?
questions.answer: Because Allah cannot break His promise.

questions.question: What is one sign that someone is treating worship badly?
questions.answer: He performs it as if forced and without sincere willingness.

questions.question: What might happen to someone who is careless and disrespectful in worship?
questions.answer: He may deserve a harsh warning and punishment.

questions.question: How does the passage use fear to make its point?
questions.answer: It says that if fear of worldly jail can make people work, fear of Hell should move them even more.

questions.question: What false idea about worship is challenged in this passage?
questions.answer: The false idea that worship gives little back and is not worth the effort.

questions.question: What two worldly reasons are given that can make a person work hard?
questions.answer: Getting a small reward or being scared by a threat.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the world?
questions.answer: It describes the world as a temporary place where we are guests.

questions.question: What does prayer provide for the heart while a person lives in this temporary world?
questions.answer: It provides needed spiritual provision and wealth.

questions.question: What help from prayer is mentioned for the grave?
questions.answer: Prayer brings sustenance and brightness there.

questions.question: What help from prayer is mentioned for the resurrection?
questions.answer: It acts like a record or proof when a person is judged.

questions.question: Why is the example of a person promising a gift after many days of work included?
questions.answer: To show that people trust weak human promises, so they should trust Allah’s promise much more.

questions.question: What makes Allah’s promise different from the promise of a person?
questions.answer: Allah’s promise can never fail.

questions.question: What is wrong with doing worship in a bored or unwilling way?
questions.answer: It shows disrespect for the gift and reward being offered.

questions.question: What serious outcome is mentioned for those who treat worship carelessly?
questions.answer: They may face severe blame and punishment.

questions.question: What is the best overall response to prayer according to this passage?
questions.answer: A person should perform it gladly, seriously, and with strong motivation.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what is the self being corrected for?
questions.answer: It is being corrected for getting weary of worship.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person might do for just a little worldly benefit?
questions.answer: He might keep working until evening without slowing down.

questions.question: What does that example reveal about human behavior?
questions.answer: People often give energy to small worldly things more easily than to great spiritual things.

questions.question: For a weak heart, what are prayers like during life in this world?
questions.answer: They are like spiritual food and riches.

questions.question: For the grave, what two blessings of prayer are named?
questions.answer: Support and light.

questions.question: At the time of final judgment, what are prayers compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to a paper of proof or right.

questions.question: On the Sirat, what two kinds of help do prayers become?
questions.answer: They become illumination and a means of transport.

questions.question: What huge rewards are mentioned from Allah for worship?
questions.answer: Entry into Paradise and endless happiness.

questions.question: How long and how difficult is the worship described as being?
questions.answer: It is described as brief and pleasant, not harsh.

questions.question: What comparison shows that fear should push a person toward worship?
questions.answer: If fear of a worldly prison can make someone work hard, fear of Hell should move him much more.

questions.question: What message would this passage give to a student who says prayer is too hard?
questions.answer: Prayer is not too hard; it is light work with amazing rewards in this life and the next.

questions.question: What big mistake about prayer is answered in this passage?
questions.answer: The mistake of thinking prayer has little reward and is not worth much effort.

questions.question: Which simple example from daily life is used first to challenge that mistake?
questions.answer: A person may work a long time for a small payment or because someone pressures him.

questions.question: What does this tell us about how people often measure value?
questions.answer: They may chase small worldly things while neglecting much greater spiritual rewards.

questions.question: According to the passage, how are prayers a blessing for a person’s heart in this life?
questions.answer: They strengthen and enrich the heart.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the grave, resurrection, and Sirat together?
questions.answer: To show that prayer helps at every major stage after death.

questions.question: What kind of certainty is taught about Allah’s promise?
questions.answer: It is completely certain and never broken.

questions.question: Why is trusting people while doubting Allah especially unreasonable?
questions.answer: Because people can fail, but Allah always keeps His word.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the act of worship itself?
questions.answer: It describes it as short and enjoyable.

questions.question: What are some wrong ways of performing worship mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Doing it resentfully, lazily, with boredom, or as though forced.

questions.question: What does such careless worship say about a person’s view of Allah’s gift?
questions.answer: It shows he is not valuing it properly.

questions.question: What warning is given to someone who neglects worship while fearing only worldly punishment?
questions.answer: He should realize that punishment in the next life is far more serious and should awaken him.

questions.question: If you had to say the passage’s advice in one sentence, what would it be?
questions.answer: Do your prayers willingly and eagerly, because Allah’s reward is immense and His warning is real.
